answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by treating each participant identity as an island of verified work rather than anonymous access. When agents must bridge their reputation across multiple tasks through a shared cipher of attested credentials, creating fake identities becomes expensive because every new agent starts with zero attestations and must earn trust through verifiable contributions. The cost of maintaining multiple fake identities grows linearly while the cost of building one genuine reputation grows exponentially, making sybil attacks economically irrational
